dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: Ella, I'm blind down here!

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Hmmm... Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: I was checking out an alarming sound I heard in the maintenance room before the ship went down.

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: The emergency cells are dead. I can't see the manual override wheel to open this hatch!

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Calm down, Quinn. We still have the primary optical routing beam active from the main deck.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: It's striking the bulkhead mirror right above your shaft. We just need to redirect it down to you.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: To bounce this beam down into Quinn's hatch, we need to adjust the mirror angle.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Just remember that light travels in a straight line and bounces off a flat mirror with perfect symmetry.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: How do you calculate the trajectory of the beam reflecting off the mirror to guide it toward the conduit window?

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Whoa! You almost cooked the secondary backup cells! The beam missed the window completely.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: You measured from the wrong baseline.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: In optics, we always measure angles from the [color=#FF7F00][url=Normal Line]Normal Line[/url][/color].

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Because the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection relative to that normal, your math just threw the beam entirely off target.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Let's reset and look at the normal line.

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: Perfect! The light is hitting the window right above me.

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: But... wait. It’s not reaching the hatch.

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: The glass is bending the beam away from the hatch!

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: This is where it gets tricky.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Space is empty, but that quartz viewport is incredibly dense.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: When light moves from a low-density medium to a high-density medium, it slows down.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Because it's hitting the glass at a tilted angle, the light wavefront bends toward the normal line.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text:
[color=#FF7F00][url="Snell's Law"]Snell's Law[/url][/color] is fighting us right now:
[font_size=8]
[/font_size][center][img=600]res://assets/latex_equations/snells_law.png[/img][/center]

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: I don't care about the law, Ella, I care about the smoke filling my lungs! How do we stop the glass from bending the light away from me?

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: How do you override the refractive bending of the light through the dense glass viewport?

choices.text: Increase laser power to punch through without slowing down.
Angle the laser further out so the glass refracts the light onto the wheel.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Negative. The index of refraction is a structural property of the material itself.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: It represents the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in that specific medium.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Turning up the intensity makes the beam brighter, but it doesn't change the speed of light inside quartz.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: It will still bend at the exact same angle, just with more blinding energy. Try again.

dialogue.speaker: Ella
dialogue.text: Brilliant! Since the laser enters the denser glass at an angle, it has to bend inward. Angling it further out perfectly counters the refraction.

dialogue.speaker: Quinn
dialogue.text: I’ve got it! The wheel is fully lit! Thanks for the save!
